plan: My private value is $25. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This means bidding $25 ensures I only win if the prize is worth more to me than what others bid. If I win, I'll pay less than my valuation. If I lose, I miss out on potential profit. With no previous round history and values drawn independently, a true-value bid seems most rational.

My private value is $3, which is quite low. Since I want to maximize profit, I should bid strategically. With only one round, I want to minimize potential losses. A low bid close to my value makes sense - if I bid too high, I risk paying more than the item is worth to me. I'll bid slightly above my value to have a small chance of winning if others bid conservatively, but not so high that I'll take a big loss.

With a private value of $26, my optimal strategy is to bid strategically to maximize potential profit. Since values are drawn independently and randomly, I'll aim to bid slightly below my true value to minimize potential overpayment. A bid around $24-$25 allows me to potentially win if other bidders bid lower, while protecting against paying too much above my actual value. I'll choose a bid that balances potential gain with risk of overpaying.
